message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: check
on: [push]
jobs:
  markdownlint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Use Node.js 18
        uses: actions/setup-node@v1
        with:
            node-version: 18
      - name: run markdownlint linter
        run: |
          npm install -g markdownlint-cli rumdl@0.3.0
          markdownlint CHANGELOG.md ROADMAP.md
          git ls-files -z -- '*.md' |
            xargs -0 -r rumdl check --no-config --no-cache --enable MD046,MD070 --
  spellchecker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: setup aspell
        run: sudo apt-get -y update && sudo apt-get -y install aspell aspell-en
      - name: run spellchecker
        run: |
          SPELLCHECK_OUT=$(cat CHANGELOG.md | aspell --lang=en --encoding=utf-8 --personal=./.aspell.en.pws list)
          echo $SPELLCHECK_OUT
          if [[ $(echo -n $SPELLCHECK_OUT | wc -c) -ne 0 ]]; then exit 1 ; fi
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs two lint/check jobs on every push with no job-level timeout. Repository CI history shows both jobs consistently complete in about 17-18 seconds, so representative successful-duration history exists, satisfying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition. The measured experiment batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) added timeout-minutes: 5 to a job and recorded 26.82% elapsed savings with all successes preserved (3/3 baseline and optimized). Adding a 5-minute timeout to both jobs gives roughly 16x headroom over observed duration, so valid slow runs are unlikely to be cut off, while runaway jobs are bounded. The change preserves all build/test coverage, adds no new network access, secrets, privileged actions, or publishing/deployment steps, and does not weaken permissions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
